en.name: Carlo Acutis
en.summary: Italian teenager and self-taught computer programmer who catalogued Eucharistic miracles online before dying of leukemia at fifteen.
en.body: Carlo Acutis was an ordinary Milanese teenager with a gift for computer programming and a deep personal devotion to the Eucharist, which he described as his "highway to heaven," attending daily Mass from childhood. Using his technical skill, he built a website cataloguing and documenting reported Eucharistic miracles from around the world, a project intended to help other young people encounter the faith through evidence and story rather than abstraction, and it was later turned into a traveling exhibition displayed in parishes internationally. He was diagnosed with acute leukemia in 2006 and died within days, at only fifteen, having reportedly offered his suffering for the Pope and the Church. His combination of ordinary modern teenage life, gaming, computers, football, with visible personal holiness made him an unusually relatable figure for young Catholics, and he was canonized by Pope Leo XIV in 2025, among the first millennials to be declared a saint.
